statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 18%, inside the low band, while Stress at 54% remains the elevated reading.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON on Tail 18%. The elevated component is Stress at 54%, carried by a long end near multi-decade highs and crude still above $90 rather than by observed Nasdaq-100 trend persistence. The narrow danger window spans the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance through the 20:00Z cash close and into the 21:00Z CME weekly futures halt.
headline: Session high handed back with VIX at its low and yields off their peak; two-way tape keeps Tail in the low band
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades 30,599.48, up 0.40% on the day against a 30,478.86 previous close, inside a 30,413.59 to 30,667.56 session range. The structural observation that matters is that the marginal new high at 30,667.56 was not held: price has come back roughly 68 points from it, after an earlier full retracement of the opening advance to the 30,413.59 low was itself bought. Both directions have been rejected, which is functioning mean reversion rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern that defines a pathological price path. The 254-point range is about 0.83%, a contained day. Tail therefore eases to 18% in the low band. Volatility corroborates that: VIX is 14.99, down 4.34% and sitting at its 14.98 session low after a 15.94 high. The bond side, the source of the week's stress, is also relenting. The 10-year yield is 5.17%, back at the bottom of its 5.16 to 5.23 daily range, one day after the 30-year reached roughly 5.43%, its highest since 2004; official H.15 constant-maturity data put the 2-year at 4.85% and the 10-year at 5.11% as of 23 September, so the long end has continued to firm through the week even as today's session gives some back. Crude is falling harder, WTI near $92.31 (-2.44%) and Brent near $104.04 (-2.40%), on reported US-Iran negotiations over a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief. Neither side has moved first, so that track is unresolved and remains a weekend headline channel. Today's U.S. data were mixed but not disruptive: August durable goods orders came in flat against a -0.4% consensus, orders ex-transportation rose 0.3%, and final September Michigan sentiment revised up to 48.1 from 47.8 while one-year inflation expectations printed 4.6%. Fed Hammack is scheduled at 18:00Z. Shared Finviz context collected at 14:12Z carries a partial status because its calendar and futures sections failed to collect; the available latest-session sections show semiconductor strength, six of seven names higher with ARM up 5.4%, against split megacaps, MSFT up 2.72% and META down 2.73%. That context is delayed and non-real-time and is not used here as evidence of current Nasdaq-100 structure. Equities higher while VIX makes a session low, yields back off and crude falls is an internally consistent easing of the week's stress, but the absolute levels of rates and energy remain the standing pressure, so Stress stays elevated at 54%. Dominant mode is mixed.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours stayed inside a narrow band: Tail between 18% and 22%, Stress between 54% and 59%, and Confidence between 86% and 88%, alternating between EA_ON and WATCH without approaching the block threshold at any point. Dominant mode rotated through mixed, normal and three trend-up readings across the European morning. The 13:00Z slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The near-term path keeps Tail inside the low and watch bands, rising to 21% across the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance and the power hour into the Friday close, which together define the narrow danger window. The defining feature of this horizon is the CME weekly futures halt at 21:00Z: the last eighteen hourly slots are halted, untradeable time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop, so Tail falls to the 9-10% range while Confidence decays from 75% to 55% as the 16:00Z observation ages. Stress stays elevated across the weekend and drifts up slightly at the end to reflect accumulated uncertainty from the unresolved US-Iran negotiation track and a long end near multi-decade highs, both of which reprice at the Sunday reopen rather than inside any hour of this horizon.
